text:
ByZachary Folk,

Forbes Staff.

A preliminary report indicated Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C., died from “aortic dissection due to arteriosclerotic cardiovascular disease,” according to an update shared by Graham’s office with multiple reporters on Sunday, after the longtime senator’s sudden death prompted an outpouring of tributes from political leaders.

President Donald Trump called Graham “one of the greatest people and Senators I have ever known,” as well as a “a true American Patriot”—years after Graham emerged as a close ally following staunch opposition to Trump during his first primary campaign in 2015 and 2016.

Graham was a mainstay on news programs and a major face of the Republican Party, and was scheduled for his 64th appearance on “Meet the Press” on Sunday morning.

Trump, who instead spoke to “Meet the Press,” said he spoke with Graham before his death, after the senator returned from a trip to Ukraine: “he sounded great actually, but he actually said he was tired.”

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., called Graham a “trusted adviser and colleague to me and many others, and numerous presidents and heads of state have relied on his counsel,” praising him for his past leadership and offering “heartfelt condolences.”

Graham was famous for his hawkish views on foreign policy, backing military support for U.S. allies like Ukraine and Israel, and both Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wrote long tributes to what the Ukrainian leader called “a true defender of freedom and the values that make our world safer.”

Later on Sunday, former President Joe Biden, another longtime veteran of the Senate, noted he and Graham “disagreed often, and sometimes loudly” but praised him for belief in the “profound importance of public service” and his love for the Senate as an institution.

Citing recordings of emergency dispatch calls, the Wall Street Journal reported that D.C.’s Fire and EMS responded Saturday evening to reports of someone facing chest pains at Graham’s address on South Capitol Street. The 911 call was made by an unidentified woman who was not at the residence. According to the report, emergency crews mentioned needing to force their way into the home because the door was deadbolted and no one answered their knocks. A later radio dispatch from the residence mentioned that responders were attempting CPR on a person who had suffered from “cardiac arrest.”

In one of the stranger tributes that came in on Sunday, FBI Director Kash Patel said his agency was “assisting local authorities and has made every necessary resource available.” Law enforcement has not indicated any evidence of foul play in the senator’s death, and unnamed law enforcement sources later told CNN that police were only conducting a normal review that typically happens after a death is reported.

South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster said his family was "devastated" and called Graham “irreplaceable” in a statement Sunday. South Carolina state law allows McMaster to immediately appoint a replacement for the rest of Graham’s term in office. Graham’s term is up in January, and he was running for reelection in November. Speaking to “Meet the Press” on Sunday, Trump said he already had a candidate in mind to fill the South Carolina seat. “It’s too soon with Lindsey,” the president said. “I don’t want to even talk about anybody. But I do have somebody that I think is really good.” Trump then heaped praise on McMaster, whom he said is “a really good governor, a really good guy,” adding, “he’s going to do the right thing, I think.” Other South Carolina Republicans also offered praise for Graham. Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., who announced her departure from Congress earlier this year in a failed bid to run for governor, wrote “whatever you thought of his politics, he carried a weight most people never have to carry.” However, Mace also faced blowback after posting a clip from “The Godfather: Part III,” featuring Al Pacino as Michael Corleone saying the famous line: “just when I thought I was out, they pull me back in.” Mace told Fox News on Sunday she will “take a look” at running to fill Graham’s seat.

Outspoken billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman on Sunday reposted a video of Graham speaking in Ukraine the previous day, noting: “This doesn’t look like a guy who would die hours later,” without directly suggesting he believed conspiracy theories of foul play largely circulating on political fringe accounts.

Graham’s office only said the senator died from a “brief and sudden illness,” initially offering no further cause of death. His family asked for “privacy during this incredibly difficult time,” according to Graham’s office. EMS responded to a call of cardiac arrest at Graham’s home in Washington, D.C., on Saturday night, according to brief audio obtained by CNN and other outlets. Speaking to “Meet the Press” on Sunday morning, Trump speculated this must have happened shortly after his call with the senator. “It must have been right after that, because I understand the police or whoever it is came there at about 7:30-8:00 in the evening… so somebody notified them.” Trump seemed surprised about Graham’s death, noting “he was fine. I knew him well. He would let you know if he wasn’t feeling well.” Graham’s office later shared a preliminary report indicating the senator died from arteriosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but his death certificate will still be pending until “until all the toxicological and microscopic testing are finalized,” the report indicated.

Trump said Graham sounded “a little bit tired, but he had a right to be” after returning from his trip to Ukraine. The president said Graham wanted to keep working to pass the Save America Act, the controversial voter ID bill Trump is trying to push through the legislature. “He was like a member of the family to me, it’s very tough,” Trump said.
